jobs.title: AI Research Intern: Foundation Models
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Summary

GrayMatter Robotics is a well-capitalized Physical AI company headquartered in Los Angeles, building Factory SuperIntelligence (FSI) through systems that learn, adapt, and develop genuine process intelligence across every part they touch. Our robots take on the tedious, hazardous, and ergonomically demanding work that has kept manufacturing dependent on a shrinking skilled workforce, delivering superhuman performance. Robotics has a demo problem. GMR doesn't. Our systems are in active production today, adapting autonomously to real geometries, real materials, and real process variation without reprogramming. We deliver our system through a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that converts capital expenditure into an operating subscription, making Physical AI accessible to the manufacturers who need it most. We hire people who want to solve hard physical problems at an industrial scale.

As the AI Research Intern: Foundation Models, you will join the Special Projects: AI team, a cross-functional group responsible for designing, building, and operationalizing AI capabilities across GMR’s products and customer deployments. The team operates end-to-end from problem formulation and data strategy to model development, simulation, deployment, and long-term performance monitoring collaborating closely with robotics software, solutions engineering, applications, process engineering, hardware, and deployment teams. The team’s mandate is to ensure that AI systems scale across processes, customers, and sites, and perform reliably on real robots in real factories, today, not just in controlled demonstrations.

What to Expect

  • Work with the Special Projects AI team to work on next generation of foundation models that power GrayMatter Robotics Solutions (FSI)

  • Take on real, complex, ambiguous problems and work through them on accelerated timelines, largely independently

  • Develop foundation models for high precision manufacturing applications with multi-modal data beyond Vision or Force alone

  • Validate models through rigorous testing on real world industrial robots and actual production parts

  • Own the entire project lifecycle: data curation, simulation, model training, evaluation and robot deployment

  • Write maintainable, production quality code for internal R&D

Export Control Requirements

In order to comply with the export regulations of the United States Government, it is required that the applicant must fall under one of the following categories: (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (i.e. current green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.

What You’ll Bring

  • Currently pursuing (remotely) a PhD in Robotics, AI, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related fields

  • Research experience in Foundation Models for robot manipulation applications

  • Proficiency in Python and at least one deep learning framework: PyTorch is preferred

  • Strong working knowledge and deep understanding of current World Models and Foundation Model Research

  • Demonstrated experience working with simulation environments and/or physics-based modeling for robotics (e.g. Isaac Lab or MuJoCo)

  • Experience with reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or policy optimization for robotic manipulation or process control

  • Experience with robotics middleware and tooling (e.g., ROS/ROS2) and deployment on real robotic hardware

  • A publication track record in venues such as ICRA, CoRL, RSS, IROS, RA-L, or T-RO, balanced with a strong bias toward real-world production impact

Nice to Have’s

  • Experience with VLA/VLM training

  • Experience with industrial manipulators and demonstration of research deployed in industrial environments

We hire people who want to solve hard physical problems at an industrial scale.

We help manufacturers improve the quality of life for their workforce while increasing production capacity, and reducing scrap, repair, and rework costs. As a Robotics Engineering Manager: Systems & Applications, you will join our Activation Team onsite in our Carson, CA office to grow our Systems & Applications Engineering (SAE) engineers—an essential group that interfaces with nearly every team across the organization.

Role & Responsibilities

As a Robotics Engineering Manager, you will…

  • Be responsible for delivering consistently high-quality engineering output and train a team of deeply capable engineers who are known industry-wide for their problem-solving rigor, systems fluency, and collaborative strength

  • Set the technical standard and lead by example: architect, debug, build, and launch physical systems

  • Adopt a hands-on approach to develop people and systems in parallel

  • Break down complex system-level issues across the hardware/software stack and guide others to solve them effectively

  • Drill into engineering output to ensure work meets the right level of quality, performance, and long-term maintainability

  • Ask the right questions to help others gain insight and move forward confidently

  • Serve as a coach and mentor; train engineers in structured problem solving and technical decision-making

  • Create onboarding and ongoing learning frameworks for new and existing SAE team members

  • Conduct performance reviews and career development conversations with empathy and clarity

  • Champion engineering best practices across the team

  • Allocate SAE resources dynamically based on cross-functional needs (Project, Product, RDO, Sales, Gov’t, CSS, Marketing)

  • Prioritize and coordinate team members’ time in alignment with evolving org-wide priorities

  • Communicate team bandwidth, skill alignment, and project risk to the broader org

  • Work closely with Product and other stakeholders to ensure clarity in handoffs, timelines, and quality expectations

  • Operate as a thought partner to technical and non-technical leaders who rely on SAE as an internal center of expertise

Export Control Requirements

In order to comply with the export regulations of the United States Government, it is required that the applicant must fall under one of the following categories: (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (i.e. current green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.

Minimum Qualifications

  • BS/MS degree or equivalent years of experience in Robotics, Automation, Advanced Manufacturing, Mechanical, Electrical, or related field

  • 6+ years experience building and launching complex physical systems (robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, etc.)

  • 2+ years experience managing performance, developing engineers and allocating team resources

  • Strong systems thinking with hands-on technical experience across the full stack: hardware, firmware, software, and integration

  • Familiarity with ROS, embedded systems, and full-stack development for robotics or automation systems

  • Ability to translate bandwidth, technical risk, and resource needs into actionable decisions

  • Track record of training, mentoring, or leveling up teams through direct teaching and role modeling

  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

  • Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively across multiple teams

  • Willingness to work in a fast-paced environment with quickly changing priorities

  • Must secure work authorization in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization beginning at the time of hire through the entirety of employment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading various distributed/multi-location teams, including external design and manufacturing partners

  • 8+ years experience building and launching complex physical systems (robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, etc.)

  • Prior experience as a Principal Engineer with formal people leadership responsibilities at a high-growth company

  • 4+ years managing engineers directly, including performance reviews and career development

  • Experience supporting multiple cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, high-growth startup or scaling environment

  • Strong organizational agility: able to manage shifting priorities, allocate bandwidth, and balance technical depth with operational decision-making

  • Experience standing up or scaling internal training programs, onboarding systems, or technical development tracks

  • Recognized internally or externally as a thought leader or technical mentor

You will lead the development of core C++ and ROS/ROS 2 components, architect high-performance subsystems, and integrate cutting-edge hardware to deliver reliable, production-ready automation solutions.

Role & Responsibilities

As a Staff C++ Architecture Engineer, you will…

  • Design and implement high-quality C++ (and some Python tooling) for ROS/ROS 2 nodes, libraries, and utilities (rcl-cpp, actions/services, components, lifecycle, launch).

  • Integrate and support sensors and actuators (cameras, LiDAR, robot controllers); develop and maintain device drivers, message interfaces, health checks, and diagnostics.

  • Architect scalable, testable subsystems (configuration, state machines, fault recovery, observability) using robust design patterns.

  • Diagnose and resolve performance and scalability challenges.

  • Own components, features, or systems with end-to-end responsibility.

  • Develop reusable software components for interfacing with back-end platforms.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams (product, design, operations, infrastructure) to create innovative application experiences.

  • Continuously improve code quality, efficiency, and performance.

  • Conduct reviews, write clear documentation, and advocate best practices for safety, reliability, and maintainability.

Export Control Requirements

In order to comply with the export regulations of the United States Government, it is required that the applicant must fall under one of the following categories: (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (i.e. current green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics or equivalent practical experience.

  • 8+ years of industry experience in developing and shipping production software in modern C++ (14/17/20).

  • Proven track record of owning and delivering components, features, or systems.

  • Familiarity with large-scale system design and architecture best practices.

  • Experience with concurrency and real-time programming.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

  • Strong skills in debugging and troubleshooting real robots/embedded systems (logs, tracing, sanitizers, core dumps).

  • Excellent communication and cross-team collaboration skills.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s or PhD in Computer Science or Robotics.

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with ROS or ROS 2 (nodes, messages, actions/services, launch, packaging).

  • Expertise in object-oriented design and API development; familiarity with SOLID principles and clean architecture.

  • Proficiency with Linux, CMake/colcon, Git, and common CI tools (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI).

  • Solid foundation in algorithms and data structures.

  • Recognized as a technical mentor or thought leader.

Role & Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement algorithms, systems, and architecture for high-DOF robotic systems working in manufacturing environments.

  • Ability to configure, troubleshoot, and develop low-latency robust interfaces for high-bandwidth, high-throughput sensor data.

  • Develop and implement computer vision and perception algorithms using multi-modal sensing for 3D geometry reconstruction, segmentation, and inspection for manufacturing applications.

  • Design and own full active perception pipelines, including exploration strategies, viewpoint planning, and coverage optimization, integrating them into robotic workflows

  • Develop high-performance production-ready software packages and systems by enabling GPU programming and other hardware acceleration methods.

  • Stay up to date with new research and novel findings in the fields of robotics and artificial intelligence.

  • Maintain current knowledge of the product and related hardware to offer technical assistance to both internal and external teams, at our facilities and customer locations.

  • Effectively identify and resolve complex and stochastic software issues through systematic debugging, ensuring optimal functionality of the system.

  • Allocate 30% of the time to assist the application team for POCs, FATs and deployments, complementing core software development responsibilities with support in application-related tasks and collaborations.

  • Travel to client locations as needed for on-site system-level debugging, ensuring the restoration and maintenance of optimal system functionality.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Robotics, Computer Science or similar engineering discipline.

  • 2+ years of demonstrated industry experience in developing, implementing, and testing algorithms for planning/learning/perception/control.

  • Experienced in developing complex function-based software that interacts with sensor inputs, control loops, and redundancy.

  • Proficiency in C++ and Python production-level coding.

  • Strong experience implementing and optimizing 3D geometry algorithms such as point cloud filtering, registration (ICP, feature-based), and segmentation.

  • Ability to fuse multi-view 2D and 3D sensor data (e.g., RGB + depth, multiple point clouds) into a single aligned point cloud or mesh.

  • Hands-on experience working with hardware vision sensors (e.g., Zivid, LMI, Ensenso, Realsense) and integrating them into existing software stacks.

  • Familiar with ML/DL methods for image and point cloud processing.

  • Proven track record of architecting perception pipelines that combine classical 3D geometry with ML/DL approaches.

  • Strong ML/DL background as a core skill — including 2D image segmentation, 3D semantic/instance segmentation of point clouds, defect detection, and combining learned with geometry-based methods.

  • Experience designing and deploying multi-sensor fusion frameworks (calibration, synchronization, merging outputs from multiple cameras) in real-world systems.

  • Ability to lead hardware–software integration efforts and ensure robustness across deployments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Robotics, Computer Science or similar engineering discipline.

  • 5+ years of experience deploying software systems in production environments.

  • Designing and owning full active perception pipelines, including exploration strategies, viewpoint planning, and coverage optimization, and integrating them into robotic workflows.

  • Create documentation, manuals, and educational content

  • Master’s degree or higher in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or related field

  • Experience programming 6DOF robots

  • Business competent (intermediate to advanced) programming knowledge in C++ and Python

  • Familiarity with motion control systems and robotics programming languages (e.g. Robot Operating System) or similar frameworks.

  • Ability to solve technical problems effectively, efficiently, and independently

  • Demonstrated experience with 3D solid modeling, analysis, and development of 2D manufacturing drawings

  • Familiar with industrial facilities and equipment

  • Effective communication skills and strong interpersonal skills to work with internal and external stakeholders

  • Willingness to travel to customer sites as required by the role

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or related field with a focus or specialization in robotics

  • Experience with sensor integration and calibration for robotics applications, including 3D vision systems, LiDAR, and inertial measurement units.

  • Be on site when the work cell is delivered to lead unboxing, setup, and customer training on the use of the system.

  • Triage, investigate, and resolve complex technical issues spanning software, hardware, sensors, and tooling, escalating with clear root cause analysis when remote resolution is not possible.

  • Respond to customer emails and calls on the use of the system, making on site service calls when issues cannot be resolved remotely, and identify new opportunities to expand impact within each account.

  • Collaborate cross functionally with Robotics Software, Hardware, and Product teams on deployments, and deliver structured feedback that improves both the product and the field engineering experience.

  • Leverage AI tools to accelerate troubleshooting, debugging, and the production of technical documentation, raising your own throughput and the team's.

  • Maintain flexible working hours that match the manufacturing production hours of customers, and travel to customer sites as needed, up to 75% of the time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2 or more years of industry experience demonstrating hands-on hardware and software skills, with experience in manufacturing automation or a similar field.

  • Willingness to travel to customer sites in Tijuana and Mexicali, up to 75% of the time, and to work with customers at their sites.

  • Effective communication and strong interpersonal skills to work with internal and external stakeholders.

  • Ability to perform multiple tasks concurrently and respond to emergency situations effectively.

  • Ability to communicate technical and complex information clearly, both verbally and in writing; documentation is key.

  • Ability to solve technical problems effectively, efficiently, and independently.

  • Demonstrated proficiency working in Linux environments and with remote support tools.

  • Professional working proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and verbal.

  • Willingness to work in a fast paced environment with quickly changing priorities.

  • Must have authorization to work in Mexico and maintain ongoing work authorization from time of hire through the duration of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Familiarity with industrial facilities and equipment.

  • Basic experience with ROS, Python, and/or C++.

  • Proficiency in 3D CAD design (any tool).

As a Strategic Sales Development Representative, you're a builder. You'll chase new opportunities, expand into new manufacturing markets, and help construct GMR's outbound sales engine from the ground floor, defining the processes that scale as the company scales. You'll keep our outbound approach current with the latest AI capabilities, so outreach at GMR stays cutting edge. This role sits within our Marketing team and creates qualified opportunities for our Account Executives.

  • Develop a deep and continually evolving understanding of GMR's products, and of how they map to the unique manufacturing processes across different industries. This role rewards a fast, voracious, curious learner who can move from product mechanics to industry-specific value in a single conversation.

  • Engage prospects consultatively: understand their business challenges, operational needs, and potential fit before you pitch anything. Treat every call like a consultation, mapping their business objectives against GMR's solutions to select the most aligned opportunities for our Account Executives. Discernment is key.

  • Build and run high-volume, multi-channel outreach (cold calling, personalized email, social) that finds inventive paths to decision-makers, testing and adopting new AI-enabled outreach tools and tactics as they emerge so GMR's outbound stays ahead of the market.

  • Book appointments and demos for the sales team, keep prospect records accurate, and translate each customer's problems and goals clearly to the AE. We believe accurate, incisive internal communication is the fuel that keeps a sales engine running smoothly.

  • We value results, not strict call volume. If your call strategy is broken, fix it. If it's winning, we'll systemize it and add it to our playbook. We want builders who think outside of the box and make the whole team better.

  • Provide regular feedback on lead quality, market conditions, and campaign effectiveness, feeding directly into how the outbound engine evolves. Adapt your approach as the team grows and strategy evolves.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Evidence of persuasion and outreach skill from any arena: launching a brand, competitive debate, fundraising, or campus organizing. Point us to content that moved an audience, cold outreach that actually landed, or anything else that makes the case for why you'll excel here regardless.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with demonstrated ability to craft a compelling message and hold your own on the phone or in an inbox.

  • 6+ months of experience operating effectively in a role with limited context and taking ownership of ambiguous problems without waiting for complete instructions.

  • Experience incorporating structured feedback in real time (call coaching, pitch reviews, manager notes) to improve performance within a role.

  • Experience working in a fast-paced or high-growth environment with frequently changing priorities or processes.

  • Strong time management and prioritization skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams to move deals forward.

  • Experience demonstrating resilience and a results-driven mindset; able to sustain motivation and a positive approach through consistent rejection.

  • You're a fast learner who absorbs new information quickly, takes feedback well, and continuously sharpens your pitch and outreach.

  • Must secure work authorization in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization beginning at the time of hire through the entirety of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 1-2+ years in a sales-oriented role, ideally as an SDR, BDR, or AE with a strong track record in outbound prospecting (cold calling, email, LinkedIn).

  • Bilingual in Spanish, written and verbal fluency.

  • Demonstrated experience with 3D solid modeling, analysis, and development of 2D manufacturing drawings; SolidWorks expert level.

  • Familiarity with motion control systems, robotics programming, and industrial facilities and equipment.

  • Ability to solve technical problems effectively, efficiently, and independently.

  • Effective communication skills and strong interpersonal skills to work with internal and external stakeholders.

  • Willingness to travel to customer sites as required by the role.

  • Must meet export control requirements in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization beginning at the time of hire through the entirety of employment.

  • 10+ years of robotic system design and integration experience.

  • Experience with industrial robot transporter design using Preston-Eastin or Güdel tracks.

  • Experience with sensor integration and calibration for robotics applications, including 3D vision systems.

The Role

GrayMatter Robotics runs physical robots at customer production sites, maintains a growing government enclave, and supports an engineering team that moves fast. Right now, too much of the IT work that keeps all of that running is falling on a DevOps engineer who should be focused on infrastructure, a QA engineer who shouldn't be configuring machines at all, and senior engineers who are getting pulled into IT requests they shouldn't have to touch.

We need one person to own that surface. Someone who can walk into an ambiguous IT situation, figure out what needs to happen, and drive it to resolution without needing to be managed through it.

That is the IT Systems Engineer. You will be the go-to for IT across the organization, covering internal infrastructure, fleet management, customer site support, and government enclave compliance. The role spans a wide range of domains on purpose. The right person is not a deep specialist. They are someone a few years into their career who has built real range across Linux, networking, and scripting, and who gets energy from variety rather than being slowed down by it. Think less "I own the firewall" and more "whatever IT problem lands here, I will figure it out."

What You Will Do

Shadow and document existing systems in the first few weeks, then take increasing ownership across:

  • Serve as the primary IT escalation point, reducing reliance on DevOps and engineering teams for routine and recurring IT requests

  • Own PC fleet management, including provisioning, imaging, Ansible-based configuration, and Teamviewer enrollment for both internal and customer site machines

  • Troubleshoot and resolve GPU driver issues and kernel update problems that cause production downtime at customer sites, then build SOPs so the fix is never tribal knowledge again

  • Support internal IT requests from all teams, including tool integrations, access management, onboarding and offboarding provisioning, and network configuration

  • Assist with government enclave maintenance, including compliance logging, access control, and working with our enclave contractor to reduce the admin overhead that currently falls on senior engineers

  • Own the IT intake process, including standing up a clear ticketing workflow and making it easy for anyone within the organization to know where to route a request

  • Work with DevOps on DevOps-adjacent tasks (CI runner uptime, VPN setup, DNS, internal tooling deployments) without needing hand-holding

  • Field customer site IT support, especially for activation machines, license servers, and network misconfigurations that require fast turnaround

  • Demonstrated ability to source, negotiate, and manage supplier contracts, including resolving delivery defaults against fixed lead-time commitments.

  • Strong skills in budgeting, cost optimization, and negotiation, paired with excellent written and verbal communication.

  • Proficiency with procurement and vendor management software and systems.

  • Must have authorization to work in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization from time of hire through the duration of employment.

When I started in 2023, we had 25 full-time employees. Today, we've more than quadrupled so, as you can imagine, I'm eager to find a teammate who's excited to build from scratch, finds joy in the details, and — above all — shares my obsession with creating a space where people are excited to show up every day.

  • There's an opportunity to build, break, and build again in a crazy-fast environment

  • You'll have a lot of influence over culture, process and our HR infrastructure

  • We are building incredible technology serving an industry that has historically been overlooked by automation...and we're the first to do it

You'll hate this role because...

  • There's an opportunity to build, break, and build again in a crazy-fast environment (not a typo)

  • A large portion of your role will be putting out fires, fielding questions and always assuming positive intent...especially when it's not easy

  • You'll be the sole HR Generalist so you'll have to iterate on the processes as we execute against our goals which will test your grit, determination, and resilience

We know startups aren't for everyone, especially this one where it is an absolute grind and a high standard of excellence. But if you're someone who deeply loves the HR function, has little patience for fixed mindsets, and is excited to get in at the ground level of one of the fastest growing robotics startups, join me on my mission to build spaces where people enjoy showing up every day, where talent thrives and the meaning of "HR" is redefined.

Role & Responsibilities

This role will own and shape the entire employee experience at GrayMatter Robotics, from onboarding to off-boarding and everything in between. This is a tactical and hands-on position ideal for someone excited to build people systems from the ground up while ensuring compliance and driving culture. Aspects of this role include:

Employee Relations & Engagement

  • Lead employee engagement efforts, including surveys, recognition, and internal communications.

  • Plan company events, offsites, and culture-building initiatives.

  • Oversee employee on-boarding, off-boarding and exit processes.

  • Partner with cross-functional partners to ensure employees have the required tools, software access and devices for their role.

  • Optimize new hire orientation and onboarding, and automate processes where possible.

Payroll & Benefits Administration

  • Run payroll end to end each cycle, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance across hourly, salaried, and contractor populations.

  • Reconcile benefits enrollment and billing against carrier invoices, catching and resolving discrepancies before they compound.

  • Administer and track all types of employee leave (e.g., FMLA, parental, PTO, disability), ensuring compliance and clear communication.

HR Compliance & Risk Management

  • Ensure compliance with employment laws across multiple states, with fluency in the distinct rules governing hourly, contractor, and salaried classifications.

  • Pull and prepare reports and documentation to support internal and external audits.

  • Maintain employee handbook and update HR policies as needed.

  • Lead investigations and handle employee relations issues responsibly.

  • Manage audit readiness and required documentation.

HR Operations & Systems

  • Serve as GMR's UKG power user and other HRIS tools: own system configuration, workflow automation, and reporting.

  • Build and maintain UKG email templates (welcome emails, manager reminders, and other lifecycle communications) so the system runs itself.

  • Own and maintain our HRIS system; ensure data integrity and analytics.

  • Optimize people processes for scale (onboarding, transitions, documentation).

  • Deliver HR metrics and insights to support decision-making.

  • Use AI and automation tools to streamline reporting, audits, and repetitive HR workflows, freeing up time for higher-judgment work.

  • Assist with other HR-related tasks and projects, including but not limited to interview scheduling, hosting candidates onsite, employee events, and other initiatives as needed.

This role is based onsite in our Carson HQ 4 days a week.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 6+ years of industry experience in HR, people operations, or similar roles.

  • 2+ years building company-wide processes from scratch within the same company.

  • 2+ years working at a technology startup or technology company.

  • Proven knowledge of multi-state employment compliance (especially California) and risk mitigation, including the distinct rules governing hourly, contractor, and salaried employees.

  • Power-user level proficiency in UKG or a comparable HRIS (e.g., ADP, Paylocity, Workday), including system configuration, reporting, and email/workflow template management.

  • Demonstrated fluency using AI tools (e.g., Claude) to accelerate day-to-day HR work, from reporting to communications.

  • Demonstrated ownership of payroll administration and benefits reconciliation.

  • Proven track record guiding managers through terminations, layoffs, and other difficult personnel decisions.

  • Excellent communication, project management, and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to build relationships and collaborate effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

  • Proven ability to think strategically and develop innovative solutions to HR challenges.

  • Must have authorization to work in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization from time of hire through the duration of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Psychology, Business Administration, Industrial-Organizational Psychology, Organizational Development, Human Resources, or a related field.

  • Experience in both startup and enterprise environments, ideally having transitioned from enterprise to startups most recently.

  • HR certification (e.g., PHR, SHRM-CP).

  • Experience using WEX, Ashby, Ethena, ClickUp, and other HR/project management tools.

  • Strong expertise in leveraging efficiency and automation tools (e.g., Notion, Scribe, Airtable, Slack integrations, HR automation platforms) to streamline workflows and scale operations.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Summary

GrayMatter Robotics is a well-capitalized Physical AI company headquartered in Los Angeles, building Factory SuperIntelligence (FSI) through systems that learn, adapt, and develop genuine process intelligence across every part they touch. Our robots take on the tedious, hazardous, and ergonomically demanding work that has kept manufacturing dependent on a shrinking skilled workforce, delivering superhuman performance. Robotics has a demo problem. GMR doesn't. Our systems are in active production today, adapting autonomously to real geometries, real materials, and real process variation without reprogramming. We deliver our system through a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that converts capital expenditure into an operating subscription, making Physical AI accessible to the manufacturers who need it most. We hire people who want to solve hard physical problems at an industrial scale.

GMR is standing up one of the most ambitious builds in company history: a largely autonomous manufacturing facility supporting a major U.S. shipbuilding program, scaling from small components today to structures up to 50 feet across within two years. This role is the single point of continuity across that multi-year build, spanning dozens of new robotic applications, a key robotics collaborator, and the path to NAVSEA qualification. We need someone who has already built something at this scale before, because a program this complex cannot be handed off in pieces.

Role & Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end delivery of a multi-year, defense-scale manufacturing build-out, including standing up the physical facility itself (permitting, layout, and utilities), through to full production qualification.

  • Coordinate ongoing production operations once qualified, not just the qualification milestone itself, so output stays on schedule as volume scales.

  • Sequence work across a growing set of robotic applications, including cutting, beveling, grinding, blasting, spraying, inspection, and material handling, so each application's output cleanly feeds the next.

  • Coordinate design and scheduling decisions between GMR's engineering teams and a key external robotics collaborator to keep interdependent workstreams aligned.

  • Own the qualification roadmap with the NAVSEA, translating federal requirements into a sequenced plan for robotic process approval.

  • Report program status, risk, and milestones to senior leadership on both the customer and GMR side, including executive and government stakeholders.

  • Identify program risk early and resolve cross-functional bottlenecks before they affect schedule, cost, or qualification timelines.

  • Build and maintain the single source of truth for program requirements, milestones, and inter-company handoffs.

  • Use AI-native tools to track program status, surface risk earlier, and keep documentation current across a fast-moving, multi-site build.

  • Travel to customer and program sites as needed, up to 25% of the time.

Export Control Requirements

In order to comply with the export regulations of the United States Government, it is required that the applicant must fall under one of the following categories: (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (i.e. current green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering field, or equivalent professional engineering experience.

  • 10+ years of experience in program or project management within complex, highly regulated engineering environments such as aerospace, automotive, maritime, or defense.

  • Demonstrated experience standing up new production capability, not just managing an existing line.

  • Proven track record managing executive-level and cross-organizational stakeholder relationships.

  • Ability to operate with significant ambiguity and evolving scope, and to turn that ambiguity into a clear, sequenced plan.

  • Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively across multiple teams.

  • Willingness to work in a fast-paced environment with quickly changing priorities.

  • Willingness to travel to customer sites as required by the role.

  • Must meet export control requirements in the United States and maintain ongoing work authorization beginning at the time of hire through the entirety of employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in maritime, shipbuilding, or naval engineering environments.

  • Experience navigating NAVSEA or other federal qualification and compliance processes.

  • Prior military engineering leadership experience, such as service academy commissioning, followed by private-industry experience.

  • Demonstrated use of AI tools to automate workflows, analyze data, or accelerate program reporting.
